text:
Ilya Mikheyev scored twice against Chicago on Nov. 5, the team he played 157 games for, and the Lightning won their eighth straight at home. It was the kind of night that sticks with a new team. He has 4 goals and 6 points in 16 games in Tampa.

The goals are running a little hot: 4 on 2.41 expected, a 17.4% shooting rate against a normal range of 12% to 17%. The bigger caution is the on-ice share. Tampa takes 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, but the Lightning are nearly seven points better without him. On a team rolling like this one, that matters less than it would elsewhere.

He's 32, undrafted, and has played for four NHL teams. Evolving-Hockey's note from last season helps explain the shape of his game: in Chicago he played with weaker teammates and against strong competition (90th percentile). He's a third-line winger who draws hard matchups and can finish. We project about 17 goals. Watch whether the finishing holds once the home streak ends; his job security lives in the hard matchups, not the goals.
headline: Mikheyev burns his old team
